**Assignment:**  
You have a set of 4 .csv files in data/homework. Each file is a timeseries of temperature and light data collected in tide pools in Oregon by Jenn Fields. Bring in all 4 files and calculate the mean and standard deviation of both temperature (Temp.C) and light (Intensity.lux) for each tide pool.

* 4 Points for the map
* 4 points for the for loop
* 2 points for proper scripting and file structure of your quarto file

## Loading libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```


## Loading data & calculating summary statistics

Getting path names to homework csv files:
```{r}
HWpath <- here("Week_13", "Data", "homework")
files <- dir(path = HWpath, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE) # saves the entire path
```

Reading in one file to glimpse and see file structure:
```{r}
#| output: FALSE
testdata <- read_csv(here("Week_13", "Data", "homework", "TP1.csv"))
glimpse(testdata)
head(testdata)
```


Using readr to read in csv files, using tidyverse to summarize mean and standard deviation of temperature and light (intensity).
```{r}
data <- read_csv(files, id = "filename") |> # id argument adds a column with the file path
  group_by(filename) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE), #calculating summary statistics after grouped by filename
            stdev_temp = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_intensity = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
            stdev_intensity = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    #cleaning up filenames to remove excess
  mutate(filename = str_remove(filename, "/Users/natalie/Desktop/UH/MBIO612/MBIO612_Fall26_NGS/Week_13/Data/homework/"),
         filename = str_remove(filename, "\\.csv")) 
data
```


Using map() to do the same thing
```{r}
data <- files |>
  set_names() |> # names each list element with its file name
  map(read_csv) |> #reads in each csv
  list_rbind(names_to = "filename") |> #file names put in "filename" column
  group_by(filename) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE), #calculating summary statistics after grouped by filename
            stdev_temp = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_intensity = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
            stdev_intensity = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  #cleaning up filenames to remove excess
  mutate(filename = str_remove(filename, "/Users/natalie/Desktop/UH/MBIO612/MBIO612_Fall26_NGS/Week_13/Data/homework/"),
         filename = str_remove(filename, "\\.csv")) 
data
```

Using a for loop to do the same thing:

Path to files:
```{r}
files <- dir(path = HWpath, pattern = ".csv")
```

Pre-allocating space for the loop:
```{r}
#| output: FALSE

# creating one row for each file and columns for filename, mean and standard deviation of temperature and intensity
hw_data <- tibble(filename = rep(NA, length(files)),
                  mean_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                  stdev_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                  mean_intensity = rep(NA, length(files)),
                  stdev_intensity = rep(NA, length(files)))

hw_data
```
Filling the table with summary statistics:
```{r}
for (i in seq_along(files)) { # loop over each file (1, 2, 3)
  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(HWpath, "/", files[i])) #reading in csv files from paths
  hw_data$filename[i] <- files[i] #adding filename to filename column
  hw_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE) #calculating mean of temperature (+ other stats below)
  hw_data$mean_intensity[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
  hw_data$stdev_temp[i] <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  hw_data$stdev_intensity[i] <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
}
hw_data <- hw_data |>
  mutate(filename = str_remove(filename, "\\.csv")) #getting rid of .csv at end of filename
hw_data
```
